context: Naoko teaches Hina-young how to make takoyaki at the ramen shop.
purpose: Aunt teaching teen cooking with fond impatience.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.en: Hina, knead the flour in. Come on.
lines.style: Bright, brassy Kansai accent. Sharp, authoritative opening. Voice carries the warmth of teaching someone she loves, not coldness. Quick, energetic pace.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.style: Bright, eager chirp. Quick attack on the yes. Eight-year-old sun-like enthusiasm, fully present. Warm and immediate, like she's already moving to do it.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.en: Turn it while you grill. Keep it moving.
lines.style: Brassy Kansai-accented teaching voice. Slightly faster, more animated than before — demonstrating the action with her tone. Firm but not harsh. The confidence of someone who's done this a hundred times.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.style: Soft, tentative. Slight rise on the question, genuine uncertainty. Warm undercurrent — she trusts her auntie but isn't sure of herself yet. A little worried but trying.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: 練習や、最初はええかげんでええ。
lines.en: It's practice, love. First time doesn't have to be perfect.
lines.style: Warm Kansai softness. Gentler than the instruction lines. Reassuring without being overly sweet. The kind of aunt-voice that makes a kid feel safe trying something hard.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.style: Bright, thrilled surprise. Open-mouthed delight. Quick, genuine. The uncomplicated joy of an eight-year-old who made something and it turned out good.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.style: Brassy, proud laugh in the voice. Playful, knowing Kansai aunt energy. A little teasing, a lot loving. She's proud of her niece and doesn't hide it.
